name: What are the differences between an attached, detached, and garage conversion ADU?

mainEntity.name: What are the differences between an attached, detached, and garage conversion ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached ADU shares a wall with the primary residence, often expanding the existing footprint. A detached ADU is a standalone structure on the property, completely separate from the main house. A garage conversion ADU transforms an existing garage into a habitable living space, often being the most cost-effective option. Each type has distinct structural, design, and permitting considerations, affecting feasibility and overall project scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached ADUs share a wall, detached ADUs are standalone, and garage conversions repurpose existing garages. Each has different design and cost implications.
